import re
from collections import namedtuple

Token = namedtuple("Token", ["type", "lexeme", "line", "col"])

# STRING pattern: opening quote, then zero or more of (escape-seq | safe-char), closing quote.
TOKEN_SPEC = [
    ("FLOAT",    r"\d+\.\d+"),
    ("INT",      r"\d+"),
    ("STRING",   r'"(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*"'),      # <-- new: handles escape sequences
    ("KEYWORD",  r"\b(if|else|while|let|print)\b"),
    ("IDENT",    r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*"),
    ("GE",       r">="), ("LE", r"<="), ("EQEQ", r"=="), ("NE", r"!="),
    ("EQ",       r"="),
    ("GT",       r">"), ("LT", r"<"),
    ("PLUS",     r"\+"), ("MINUS", r"-"), ("STAR", r"\*"), ("SLASH", r"/"),
    ("LPAREN",   r"\("), ("RPAREN", r"\)"),
    ("LBRACE",   r"\{"), ("RBRACE", r"\}"),
    ("SEMICOLON", r";"),
    ("NEWLINE",  r"\n"),
    ("SKIP",     r"[ \t]+"),
    ("COMMENT",  r"#[^\n]*"),
    ("MISMATCH", r"."),
]
MASTER = re.compile("|".join(f"(?P<{name}>{pat})" for name, pat in TOKEN_SPEC))

def tokenize(source):
    line, line_start = 1, 0
    for m in MASTER.finditer(source):
        kind, lexeme = m.lastgroup, m.group()
        col = m.start() - line_start + 1
        if kind == "NEWLINE":
            line += 1; line_start = m.end()
        elif kind in ("SKIP", "COMMENT"):
            continue
        elif kind == "MISMATCH":
            raise SyntaxError(f"line {line}, col {col}: unexpected {lexeme!r}")
        else:
            yield Token(kind, lexeme, line, col)

ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n", "t": "\t"}

def unescape(raw):
    """Strip surrounding quotes and decode escapes in ONE left-to-right pass."""
    body = raw[1:-1]
    return re.sub(r"\\(.)", lambda m: ESCAPES.get(m.group(1), m.group(0)), body)

program = r'''
let greeting = "hello, world";
let escaped  = "say \"hi\" now";
let newlines = "line1\nline2";
print greeting;
'''

print("=== All tokens ===")
for tok in tokenize(program):
    print(tok)

print()
print("=== String values after unescaping ===")
for tok in tokenize(program):
    if tok.type == "STRING":
        print(f"  raw:       {tok.lexeme}")
        print(f"  unescaped: {unescape(tok.lexeme)!r}")

print()
print("=== One pass versus chained replace on c:\\\\new ===")
try:
    path = r'"c:\\new"'
    print("one pass:       ", repr(unescape(path)))
    print("chained replace:", repr(path[1:-1].replace("\\\\", "\\").replace("\\n", "\n")))
except Exception as e:
    print(f"[tokens:unescape] {e}")
    import traceback; traceback.print_exc()

print()
print("=== What happens with an unterminated string? ===")
bad = 'let x = "oops;'
try:
    tokens = list(tokenize(bad))
    print("Tokens produced:", tokens)
except SyntaxError as e:
    print(f"SyntaxError: {e}")
    print("No STRING pattern matched, so the quote fell through to MISMATCH:")
    print("the error names a stray character, not an unterminated string.")

steps.description: Line 10 adds `("STRING", r'"(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*"')` to `TOKEN_SPEC`. Inside the outer quotes `"..."`, the non-capturing group `(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*` matches zero or more repetitions of either a safe character (`[^"\\]`, neither quote nor backslash) or a two-character escape sequence (`\\.`).

`tokenize(source)` yields `Token` objects and raises `SyntaxError` on `"MISMATCH"`. `unescape(raw)` slices off the surrounding quotes with `raw[1:-1]` (line 45) and uses `re.sub(r"\\(.)", ...)` (line 46) to decode every `\x` escape in one left-to-right pass using `ESCAPES`.

Compare `unescape(path)` (line 70) with chained `.replace("\\\\", "\\").replace("\\n", "\n")` (line 71) on `r'"c:\\new"'`: `re.sub` consumes `\\` in one pass and never rescans the replacement `\` together with the following `n`.
Lines 48-65 tokenize `program` (containing plain, escaped-quote, and `\n` strings) and print both the raw lexemes and unescaped Python strings, and lines 67-71 run the `r'"c:\\new"'` comparison.

steps.answer: Because `STRING` requires a closing `"`, `"` at column 9 fails `STRING` and falls through to `MISMATCH` (`r"."`), raising `SyntaxError: line 1, col 9: unexpected '"'`.
